subject: Access & Data Controls follow-up for FinHealth (PII, RBAC, support access)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Access controls & data handling — quick recap and next steps

Hi Emma / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of the items we discussed and the concrete next steps from our side so you can review with the security team: 

Summary of requirements we captured:
- PII scope: names, DOB, last 4 SSN, limited payment metadata. No unredacted full SSNs to be stored.
- Data residency: primary workload must remain in us-west-2; backups stored in encrypted buckets in us-west-2 only.
- Retention: 90 days for raw inputs, 365 days for derived telemetry; ability to override per-customer via API.
- Logging/audit: request/response hashes + correlation IDs stored; full request bodies redacted for PII in logs and only available in encrypted archives for incident triage.
- Access controls: RBAC with least-privilege roles, SCIM provisioning, JIT break-glass for support with recorded sessions and time-bound credentials.

Deliverables we agreed to share by EOD Wednesday (my target):
1) RBAC matrix template mapping FinHealth roles -> Redwood roles (attached: redwood_rbac_template.xlsx).
2) Support access playbook describing break-glass, approval flow, session recording (attached: support_access_playbook.pdf).
3) Redacted SOC2 summary and current evidence list (attached: soc2_summary_redacted.pdf).
4) A short diagram of network/region controls + SAML/SCIM provisioning notes (I will drop a Drive link).

Questions I left for you to confirm:
- Do you need HSM-backed key management (we support AWS KMS or customer-managed keys via BYOK)?
- Is the 90/365 retention window negotiable per dataset or fixed for all PII?

Next steps:
- Emma/Rajesh: confirm whether FinHealth requires customer-managed keys and whether the retention windows are flexible.
- Jordan/Marissa: deliver attachments and Drive diagram by 2025-09-03 EOD.
- Vivek: validate break-glass workflow against usual FinHealth escalation patterns; we can iterate.

If this looks right, I’ll queue up a short follow-up call next week to walk through the RBAC matrix and support playbook with your security team.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Emma/Rajesh — adding a few technical clarifications on the RBAC and provisional templates so you can push to your IAM team: 

- Redwood role model (short):
  * admin: full org-level access (rare; used for initial onboarding).
  * engineer: deploy/inspect logs for non-PII-only workloads (no access to raw PII).
  * security_analyst: audit logs, create/approve break-glass incidents (read-only for responses).
  * support_agent: ephemeral access via JIT, screen-recorded, time-limited, approved by on-call security.

- Enforcement: we support SCIM for user provisioning + attribute-based access (department, team, environment). We recommend SCIM + SAML SSO for deterministic mapping.

- Break-glass mechanics (high-level):
  1) Support requests create a ticket (HubSpot/Jira) with justification and TTL.
  2) If PII access required, request escalates to security_analyst approval.
  3) Upon approval, Redwood issues a time-bound credential (min(1 hour, specified TTL)) and starts session recording.
  4) All activity is logged, recordings stored encrypted with access only to the security_analyst and customer-appointed auditor.

- Auditability: logs contain correlation_id, request_id, caller_identity, action, and a hashed pointer to the full request stored in encrypted archive. Retrieval requires a documented incident request.

Attachment notes: redwood_rbac_template.xlsx includes a sample mapping for FinHealth roles -> API scopes. If you want, I can pre-fill the sheet with likely mappings based on your org chart if you share titles.

I’ve also attached a short runbook excerpt in the Drive link for quick review.

Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Emma / Rajesh — quick note from the security side on a few items you asked about during the call: 

1) Customer-managed keys: we support AWS KMS CMKs with key policies that constrain usage to Redwood service principals in your account and require dual-approval for deletion. If you require an HSM appliance, we have an on-prem integration option (requires private deployment).

2) Session/recording retention for break-glass: default retention for session recordings is 180 days; can be shortened to 30/90 on request. Recordings are stored encrypted and access is controlled via RBAC (only security_analyst & customer-approved auditors).

3) Least-privilege checklist (practical):
- Enforce SCIM user attributes (role, team) at provisioning time.
- Use scoped API keys for machine-to-machine integrations (rotate every 30 days by default).
- Require MFA for all accounts with admin or security_analyst roles.
- Alerts: anomalous access triggers (geo, volume, time-of-day) route to on-call security and create an automatic break-glass review ticket.

4) Evidence we can share immediately (redacted): SOC2 summary (attached), recent penetration test triage (summary available on request), and our access-control design doc (we can write a short customer-facing extract).

If you can confirm whether FinHealth will require customer-managed KMS and whether recordings should be kept 30/90/180 days, we’ll finalize the RBAC matrix and runbook. We can also schedule a 30-minute session with our IAM engineer if you prefer a deeper walkthrough.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

Jordan / team — thanks for the detailed follow-up and attachments. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- FinHealth prefers customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for production PII. Please include the CMK integration notes and key policy example in the Drive doc.
- Retention: we are fine with the 90/365 as a starting point; would like the option to request shorter retention for sensitive subsets (e.g., financial account numbers).
- Session recordings: 90-day retention is our preferred default, but we will finalize after seeing the playbook.

Can you also provide an estimated timeline for a short technical walkthrough and an updated quote if CMK support is required? We’re targeting a pilot by end of Q4 and would like to surface this to procurement next week.

Thanks,

Emma Li
Director of Engineering | FinHealth
